identity.tagline: Interdisciplinary research leader in AI ethics, creative technologies, and civic innovation

profile.core: Professor Andy Miah is an internationally recognised academic leader with 18 years of Professorial experience across Arts & Humanities, Science & Engineering, and Health Sciences. His research in the ethics of emerging technologies spans creative industries, AI, digital sport, and health — always with a commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration and societal impact.

variants.esports: One of the UK's leading academic voices on esports, digital sport, and competitive gaming. With over a decade of sustained research, advisory, and governance work in the esports sector, he combines scholarly rigour with practical industry engagement — advising governing bodies, federations, and governments on the ethical, cultural, and technological dimensions of esports.
variants.creative-manchester: An interdisciplinary research leader with over 20 years embedded in the Greater Manchester creative and civic ecosystem. He has led major platform-building initiatives connecting academia, industry, cultural institutions, and policy — including a £4.5m Innovate UK Accelerator mobilising 250+ GM businesses into a CreaTech innovation ecosystem.
variants.science-communication: An award-winning science communicator and public intellectual with over 450 invited talks in 50+ countries. Director of The Science Communication Space at Salford and recipient of the Josh Award for Science Communication (Science and Industry Museum, Manchester, 2015).
variants.ai-ethics: A leading voice on AI ethics and emerging technologies, advising the UK Government's DCMS College of Experts, the Greater Manchester AI Foundry, and international organisations. His work spans AI ethics, biotechnology, immersive media, and digital futures.
variants.bioethics: A foundational figure in the bioethics of human enhancement, gene doping, and posthumanism. His book Genetically Modified Athletes (Routledge, 2004) remains a core text in the field, and his research has influenced government select committee inquiries and international sporting governance.
